security_audit.summary: All 117 static findings are false positives involving Markdown, documented development commands, local tests, public documentation, binding access, or an event counter. One semantic finding identifies authentication middleware that accepts any nonempty authorization header without validating credentials. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or system reconnaissance.

remediation.issue: The custom auth example in SKILL.md:321-327 checks only whether an Authorization header exists.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the presence-only check with bearerAuth or verified JWT authentication, and test missing, arbitrary, malformed, expired, and valid credentials.

content.user_title: Build and Test Hono Web Applications
content.value_statement: Hono development requires consistent routing, validation, runtime configuration, and testing patterns. This skill provides inline API guidance and CLI workflows for building typed applications.
actual_capabilities: Guide route registration, path parameters, grouping, response methods, and error handling.
Explain middleware order, request-scoped variables, and shared environment types through factories.
Show request validation with Zod and Standard Schema integrations.
Provide Hono CLI workflows for route inspection, stateful batch tests, and regression snapshots.
Demonstrate typed RPC clients, streaming responses, server-sent events, and basic JSX syntax.
Explain generated Cloudflare binding types and runtime-specific adapter imports.
limitations: This is a Markdown reference, not a bundled runtime, test suite, or executable application.
CLI workflows require project dependencies and execution access; fetching current documentation also requires network access.
Complete JSX application setup is delegated to the separate hono-jsx skill; version-specific examples require compatibility checks.
Examples require security review; the custom authentication sample checks header presence without validating credentials.

use_cases.title: Create a Validated API
use_cases.description: Build grouped routes with typed parameters, request validation, consistent responses, and local endpoint tests.

use_cases.title: Configure Worker Bindings
use_cases.description: Use the existing Cloudflare toolchain to generate binding types and select the appropriate local testing runtime.

use_cases.title: Check Route Regressions
use_cases.description: Capture existing responses, replay batch assertions after changes, and inspect differences without manually starting an HTTP server.

prompt_templates.title: Add a First Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a GET /health route to this Hono project. Return a simple success response and verify it using the existing Hono CLI.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: add one endpoint to an existing project

prompt_templates.title: Validate Request Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a POST /posts endpoint with a required title using the existing validator. Test valid, missing, and empty titles with explicit status assertions.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Typed Worker Bindings
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this project's Cloudflare configuration. Generate binding types with its existing toolchain and test a KV-backed route locally without creating remote resources.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Typed API Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Snapshot this API, refactor routes into feature groups, and preserve chained RPC types. Verify credentials, then replay stateful batch tests with isolated test bindings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: preserve behavior and type inference during refactoring

output_examples.input: Describe the expected checks for a new validated post endpoint.
output: Missing or empty title: validation rejects the request.
CLI batch assertions cover successful and invalid submissions.

output_examples.input: Outline a regression workflow before reorganizing existing routes.
output: Capture current route responses as snapshot expectations.
Refactor routes while preserving paths and chained types.
Replay expectations against isolated test state and inspect failed assertions.

output_examples.input: Review the custom authentication middleware example.
output: The example checks whether an authorization header exists, not whether credentials are valid.
Use credential verification before allowing access to protected routes.
Test missing, arbitrary, malformed, expired, and valid credentials.

best_practices: Read current Hono documentation and CLI help, then check examples against installed framework and runtime versions.
Generate binding types with the existing project toolchain and use isolated local state for request and batch tests.
Preserve chained routes for RPC inference, validate request data, and verify authentication credentials before continuing.
anti_patterns: Treating any nonempty Authorization header as proof of identity.
Running state-changing tests against production bindings or placing credentials in CLI arguments.
Mixing incompatible runtime imports or hand-writing binding types that the project toolchain generates.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does this skill install Hono automatically?
faq.answer: The file provides instructions rather than an installer. An assistant following the workflow may install the Hono CLI if it is missing.

faq.question: Can I test endpoints without starting a server?
faq.answer: Yes. app.request() dispatches requests in-process, and Hono CLI provides request and batch workflows. Some project configurations use Vite or Workers runtimes.

faq.question: Does it cover Cloudflare Workers?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains binding configuration, generated types, and local runtime selection for projects using cf or Wrangler.

faq.question: Does it include complete JSX application guidance?
faq.answer: No. It covers JSX syntax and basic rendering examples, then refers complete UI workflows to the separate hono-jsx skill.

faq.question: Are the authentication examples ready for production?
faq.answer: No. The custom middleware only checks header presence. Replace it with credential verification and test both accepted and rejected requests.
